transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... my family made me come in. I just... I keep telling them I’m the reason my friend died. I didn’t call her back when I should have, and... well, I had ugly thoughts sometimes. Now I just know the Lord is punishing everybody at our church because of me. That's what I keep telling them, anyway.
Do you genuinely feel guilty about not calling your friend back?

Yes, I do. I just... I know it's my fault she died. If I had just called her back, maybe things would be different. And like I said, I had those ugly thoughts sometimes. It's just clear to me that I'm the reason she's gone, and now... now the Lord is punishing everyone at our church because of what I did. I just feel awful about it all the time.
Do you find yourself having these ugly thoughts repeatedly, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Well, no, not really. It's not like I'm trying to stop them and they just keep coming back or anything. I just... I had them, and they were bad, and now I know that's why she's gone. It's not a repeating thing, it's just what happened.
Do you feel sad most of the time?
Yes, I do. It's just... a very heavy feeling. It doesn't really ever go away, I just feel low all day long.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being responsible for your friend's death and the Lord punishing everyone are intrusive, meaning they come into your mind without you wanting them to?

No, not really. It's not like they force their way into my head against my will or anything like that. It's just... it's just the truth. I think about it because it's what is actually happening. It's not some unwanted thought popping up out of nowhere, it's just the reality of what I've done.
Do you feel like you need to do something to make up for what you think you've done?

No, not really. I don't... there's nothing I can do to make up for it anyway. What's done is done. I don't have some urge to go out and try to fix it, because you just can't fix something like this. I just have to live with knowing it's my fault, and that's that.
Do you feel like you're spending a lot of time thinking about these thoughts of guilt and responsibility?

I don't know if I'd say I spend a lot of time thinking about it on purpose. It's just... always there. Like a dark cloud hanging over me. I'm not sitting around obsessing over it, but it's just the reality of my life now. It's hard not to think about it when it's the truth.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes. I don't... I don't do much of anything anymore. I used to love going to choir practice, and my knitting circle. I'd go to bingo, take walks through Patterson Park... but now, I just sit in my chair. None of it even feels worth getting dressed for. I just don't have it in me.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Yes, I have. My skirts have all gotten loose lately. I just don't have much of an appetite anymore. Food tastes like cardboard to me now. Most days, I just pick at a piece of toast or maybe have some tea, even when my niece makes a whole plate of food and puts it right in front of me. I just can't bring myself to eat it.
Do you hear voices or see things that other people can't?
No, I don't. I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there. It's really just my own thoughts in my head. So, no, nothing like what you're asking about.
Do you believe that the Lord is actually punishing everyone at our church because of what you did?

Yes, I do. I know He is. I keep telling them that I’m the reason my friend died. I didn’t call her back when I should have, and... I had ugly thoughts sometimes. So yes, I know the Lord is punishing everybody at the church because of me. It's all my fault.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been going on for about two months now. Ever since... well, ever since my close friend died. That's when all of this started.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide?

No, I haven't. I don't have thoughts like that. I mean... I know I'm a terrible person for what happened, and I deserve the punishment the Lord is giving me, but... no, I haven't thought about ending my own life or anything. I don't want to die.
Do you feel like your low mood is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?
I would say it's severe. Yes, definitely severe most of the time. It just feels... very heavy, like I can't get out from under it.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

No, not anymore. I used to... well, I used to love going to choir, and my knitting circle. I'd play bingo, or go walking through Patterson Park. But now I just sit in my chair. None of it feels worth getting dressed for.
Are there any small things that still bring you a little bit of joy or happiness?

No, not really. Like I was just saying, I don't do any of the things I used to enjoy. The choir, my knitting group, bingo, my walks in the park... I don't care about any of it now. I just sit in my chair all day. There's just no joy left in anything.
Do you find that you're moving more slowly than you used to?

I don't think so. I mean, since I just sit in my chair most of the day, I'm not really moving around enough to notice. But when I do get up... no, I don't think I'm moving any slower than usual. I'm just not moving much at all.
Are you unable to experience pleasure from activities that you once found enjoyable?

Yes. Like I was just saying a minute ago, I really don't get any enjoyment out of them anymore. I used to love going to my choir, the knitting circle, playing bingo, or walking through Patterson Park... but now, yes, I'm just unable to feel any pleasure from it. None of it even feels worth the effort of getting dressed for. I just stay in my chair.
